item: An interrupted Thread.start() no longer gives a live job's or damage-record's record back
summary: BackgroundJob.start() marked a job error and DamageRegistry._single_flight dropped its key when Thread.start() raised a BaseException, on the premise that the thread never ran; an interrupt during start()'s wait for the new thread leaves the thread created and about to run (ident still None), so a second worker of the same kind, or a second thread for the same key, could run beside the first (measured, peak 2). Both now act on an Exception only. Same class as #1645; BackgroundScheduler._start_detached pinned Exception-only.
